title: Greensburg, Kansas · May 4, 2007
summary: The May 4, 2007 tornado crossed from Comanche County into Kiowa County and devastated Greensburg. Follow its reported warnings, damage and dated recovery through two retained county records, original NWS accounts and documentary source links.

observations.title: One tornado across two county records
observations.locator: 35934 narrative and continuation fields;35937 opening narrative
observations.account: The Comanche record explicitly identifies the beginning of the Greensburg tornado and its continuation into Kiowa County. The Kiowa record describes the same tornado crossing the county boundary at 2003 CST / 2103 CDT.
observations.limits: The explicit documentary continuation supports one event association. Shared episode 5918 is supporting context. Each record, local damage rating, clock and endpoint remains separate.

observations.title: Oil tanks and trees in Comanche County
observations.account: The tornado began in Comanche County, where the source reports damage to oil tanks and trees. It assigns EF1 to those damaged objects and describes oil spread over pastures and a county road.
observations.limits: This local damage classification is not the maximum rating of the later tornado. The narrative does not establish an oil-release volume, camera location or surveyed route.

observations.title: From homes south of town into Greensburg
observations.locator: Event 35937 narrative, impact and property fields
observations.account: The Kiowa record describes destroyed homes and a church south of Greensburg, then destruction across nearly 95 percent of the town. It reports 961 homes and businesses destroyed, 216 with major damage and 307 with minor damage. Its reported damage estimate is about $250 million including uninsured losses.
observations.limits: These are source reported damage categories and a nominal historical estimate. No independently assessed building inventory, present day value, complete local EF5 swath or uniform wind field is inferred.

observations.title: The reported loop northwest of Greensburg
observations.account: The source describes the tornado turning north and northwest, then west, south and east as it weakened northwest of Greensburg. It attributes the looping interpretation to Doppler radar and ground-survey evidence. The same narrative describes a new circulation growing northeast of town.
observations.limits: Atlas has not independently reviewed those original radar scans or survey sheets. The description is not plotted into a new route, and the later circulation is not automatically joined to this tornado.

observations.title: The event start and the county entry have different times
observations.locator: Both record time objects and 35937 CST/CDT statement
observations.account: The Comanche record runs from 20:00 to 20:03 in its stated CST-6 convention. The Kiowa record runs from 20:03 to 21:05 under the same convention. These convert to 9:00 to 9:03 p.m. and 9:03 to 10:05 p.m. CDT, or 02:00 to 02:03 and 02:03 to 03:05 UTC on May 5.
observations.limits: These are reported source boundary minutes. The conversion does not measure physical formation, a particular building impact or camera accuracy. Retrospective warning labels remain separately attributed.

observations.title: The documented continuation has mismatching endpoints
observations.account: The Comanche ending is reported at longitude -99.4517, latitude 37.3668. The Kiowa beginning is reported at longitude -99.3826, latitude 37.3934. Their clock boundaries match, but these coordinates differ.
observations.limits: The source association is preserved without repairing either coordinate or drawing an interpolated connecting segment. No measured error bound or preferred corrected point is established.

observations.title: Segment fields and a whole-event summary
observations.account: The NWS fact sheet reports a duration of 65 minutes, a whole path of 28.8 miles and a maximum width of 1.7 miles. It gives about 205 mph as an approximate strongest surface wind in parts of town.
observations.limits: The two county records separately retain lengths of 3.01 and 25.8 miles, and Kiowa reports a maximum width of 3,000 yards. Rounding, scope and estimation stay explicit. Damage width is not visible funnel diameter, and the wind figure is not a direct measurement at every location.

observations.title: Different warning messages preceded arrival
observations.account: The NWS retrospective gives 8:55 p.m. for the first warning associated with the tornado, 9:19 p.m. for the first warning specifically naming Greensburg and 9:45 p.m. for arrival at the south side of town. Its reported 26 minutes of lead time compares the last two labels.
observations.limits: A time zone is not printed beside these retrospective labels. They are not independently recovered product bytes or evidence of individual receipt, shelter action or a measured number of lives saved.

observations.title: The event record includes a later death update
observations.locator: Event 35937 impacts and final dated note
observations.account: The Kiowa event record reports 11 direct deaths and 63 direct injuries. Its final note says that the eleventh victim died on September 19, 2007 from a head injury sustained during the tornado.
observations.limits: This event record scope is distinct from city limit, other county and wider outbreak totals. The delayed note does not establish the scope or cause of every difference in another publication.

observations.title: City limits and other counties are separate scopes
observations.account: The city page reports ten fatalities within Greensburg city limits. It separately names one death in rural Pratt County and one in Stafford County. The page also describes community meetings and a recovery plan guided by a FEMA team.
observations.limits: The other county deaths are not added to the retained Greensburg event record. The current page does not reconcile its city count with NCEI or date every recovery quantity.

observations.title: Hazardous-material response after the tornado
observations.account: EPA reports sending response staff on May 5. Early work included fuel releases, chlorine cylinders, anhydrous ammonia and propane tanks. A FEMA assignment on May 9 covered oil, hazardous material, household hazardous waste and discarded appliances. Curbside collection began on May 11.
observations.limits: These are agency-reported response and collection stages. The profile is now marked inactive. No complete cleanup, current safety determination, measured exposure or property level clearance is established.

observations.title: Recovery figures describe a dated stage
observations.account: The NWS/FEMA recovery table dated April 25, 2008 reports 800,000 cubic yards of debris removed. The report describes utilities being reconstructed after the destruction.
observations.limits: The retained Kiowa narrative separately reports about 400,000 cubic yards removed in its July 26 context. The sources are not treated as one simultaneous measurement. Neither figure establishes present recovery completion.
